subject: Art & Design
title: Proximity: Group Related Things Together
description: A quick win: understand Proximity: Group Related Things Together.

hook.text: A phone number next to the wrong name on a business card creates instant confusion. That's a proximity failure.

buildup.text: Proximity means related items should be physically close. Unrelated items should have space between them.

discovery.text: The brain automatically groups nearby elements. White space between groups signals 'these are different.'

twist.text: Adding space is as important as removing it. Proximity is about creating meaningful clusters.

climax.text: On a form, labels must be closer to their input field than to the next label. Obvious, often violated.

punchline.text: If it belongs together, put it together. Space is meaning.

quiz.question: What does proximity communicate in a layout?
options: Nearby elements are related; spaced elements are different

details.summary: Proximity groups related items together and separates unrelated items through spatial distance. Elements placed close together are perceived as belonging together; elements spaced apart are seen as distinct groups.
details.whyItMatters: Proximity is the most natural way to organize information because the brain automatically groups nearby objects. Proper use of proximity reduces cognitive effort and makes complex information instantly scannable.
takeaways: Nearby elements are perceived as belonging together
Spacing separates unrelated items into distinct groups
Proximity organizes information without labels or dividers

faq.question: How much space creates separation between groups?
faq.answer: The gap between groups should be noticeably larger than the gap within groups — typically at least 1.5 to 2 times larger. The exact measurement depends on the design's scale, but the principle remains: inter-group spacing must clearly exceed intra-group spacing.

faq.question: Can proximity override other grouping cues?
faq.answer: Often yes. Even if elements differ in color or shape, placing them close together makes them feel related. Proximity is one of the strongest Gestalt grouping principles. Designers must be careful that spatial relationships don't accidentally create wrong groupings.
